👻 Started playing for fun, stayed for the emotional damage

I've been playing Phasmophobia since it first came out, and honestly, what a journey it's been. 😂

This game has given me some of my scariest gaming moments, but also some of the BEST memories I'll ever have. I've made actual friends through this game, people I probably never would've met otherwise. And for that alone, this game will always have a special place in my heart. ❤️

The funniest part? Back in the day, I used to WALK WITH THE GHOST. Just casually following it around like we were besties. No fear, no survival instincts, just vibes. 💀

Nowadays? The front door closes in front of me and suddenly I'm fighting for my LIFE. My heart rate goes through the roof, my teammates are screaming, everyone's running in different directions, and somehow I'm still the one who dies first. Character development, I guess.

I've had moments in this game that genuinely made me question why I willingly put myself through this. But I've also laughed until I couldn't breathe, screamed so loudly I probably scared my neighbors, and made memories I'll never forget.

And that's what makes Phasmophobia so special. It's not just about finding ghosts. It's about the chaos, the friendships, the unexpected jump scares, and the absolutely questionable decisions you and your friends make at 3 AM.

So, get your confident pants on (bring a second pair, JUST IN CASE), grab your equipment, and go find that ghost.

What's the worst that could happen?

...Don't answer that. The front door just closed. I'M OUT. 🏃‍♀️💨👻

I never in a million years thought I’d be the one writing a review for Phasmophobia. Honestly, I never thought I’d actually play this game in the first place! 😂

I’m exactly the kind of person who hates horror movies, let alone horror games. At least with movies, you can cover your eyes, but here? You actually have to willingly walk into a haunted house yourself! 😂

I bought this game for my boyfriend a few years ago, but he only really got into it recently. He got absolutely hooked, and somehow managed to drag me into it too. And I have to say just one thing – THIS GAME IS AMAZING! 🤩

I’m having an absolute blast playing it! The game feels incredibly well-designed, the atmosphere is fantastic, and I absolutely love figuring out which ghost we’re dealing with. You have to think, gather evidence, and piece everything together. And the more you get into it, the more it pulls you in.

And yes, of course, I spend the entire time scared shitless. 😂 Every creak, every sound, and every unexpected event scares the living daylights out of me. But hey, that’s just who I am. I’m a total scaredy-cat! 😂

Anyway, I wholeheartedly recommend this game! ❤️ And if you’re anything like me and usually can’t stand horror games, but feel like trying something new, you might be just as surprised as I was. Just be prepared to get scared of your own shadow. 😂

Phasmophobia is truly one of the best ghost games if you're willing to learn and explore various types of ghosts, learn the layout of various maps, and be frightened upon entering a round. While it's great solo, it's even better with friends. Not only is it less boring and terrifying, you can have the best laugh and goof around with each other whilst the ghost is hunting. Do you want to have a good laugh? A good scare? Maybe even die in the most goofiest way possible? Phasmophobia is for you! 

However, like most games, Phasmophobia can have its bugs and repetitive gameplay if you've played the game long enough. Certain layouts, such as buying items, can be extremely confusing for new players. Even with a tutorial set in place, some players get confused with equipping bought items. Not only this, but there are A LOT of ghosts compared to maps. It's hard to learn every ghost if you're just starting out, and can get overwhelming really quick.

Despite Phasmophobia having its ups and downs as a game, it's overall amazing. Starting out may be terrifying and overwhelming, but as you learn the loops, it becomes fun and exciting. Especially if you're willing to spend time hunting down the ghosts and learning how the gameplay works.

When Phasmophobia first came out, I played constantly. It was genuinely scary in a way that not many games manage to pull off, especially when playing with friends. There were nights when it scared me enough that I actually had nightmares afterward.

And somehow I kept coming back.

A huge part of what made the game so much fun was playing with my friends. Unfortunately, once they stopped playing, I eventually stopped too.

I probably would have come back at some point, but one of the major reworks wiped my high level and all of the equipment I had spent so much time earning. I understand games change during development, but after putting that many hours into the original progression, I just don’t have the patience to grind everything out again.

I have a lot of great memories with Phasmophobia, though. At its best, being terrified with a group of friends while someone panics and gets everyone killed is hard to beat.

"Look how they massacred my boy" This game was peak, it was GOATed, it was a downright good time with the boys. My friend and I started playing this together years ago and seemingly with every update they introduced more bugs and more bloat that made it unplayable for me without VR and unplayable for my friend who has VR. We loved this game.

We just started playing a new game called The Other Side. It has the same gamemode as Phasmo but it features another gamemode which is so much more fun. The RE4 attaché case system in The Other SIde allows for more varied builds and the only thing missing is a VR mode. I also appreciated the progression system in Phasmo where you unlock better quality gear but in The Other Side you have all the equipment available to you form the start and the upgrades come in the form of new bases and new vehicles so you can store more of your equipment in the attaché.

If you are disappointed in the trajectory of Phasmophobia and are itching for a good ghost hunting experience with the boys check out The Other Side. The developers of that game seem to care about it more and the updates actually address bugs. I picked up two copies for approximately $17 while on it was on sale for me and my ghost hunting friend. As for Phasmophobia? Stay away from this shell of its former self rotting corpse of a game.
